sections.subtitle: The investment thesis: rate base growing off an expanding, data-center-driven capital plan

customers.title: Total customers
customers.content:
Customers is the metered connection count across Ameren's regulated electric and gas franchises in Missouri and Illinois.

For Ameren Corporation: roughly 2.5m electric and 0.9m gas connections; organic customer growth is low single digits. The rate-base growth story here is not driven by adding customers -- it comes from large-load (data center) demand on the existing franchise and grid-modernization/transmission capex approved in rate cases, which raise revenue per customer rather than the customer count.

What to watch:

  • Whether the ~2.8 GW of signed large-load agreements (Missouri) begin energizing on schedule (H2 2027 onward)
  • Customer growth staying flat while revenue and rate base grow -- confirms the regulatory/capex thesis rather than volume growth

salesVolume.title: Electric sales volume
salesVolume.content:
Sales volume is total electric GWh delivered across Ameren's franchises, FY-only (weather and the fuel pass-through make quarterly comparisons noisy).

For Ameren Corporation: volume growth is the first confirmation that the signed large-load (data-center) contracts are actually energizing -- management's plan calls for 2.9 GW of incremental Missouri load by 2030. Revenue can rise faster than volume because rate increases, not just usage, drive the top line in a cost-of-service model.

What to watch:

  • A step-up in GWh once the 2.8 GW of signed large-load demand begins energizing (H2 2027)
  • Weather-driven swings in residential/commercial volume versus the structural large-load trend

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Ameren Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Ameren Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Ameren Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Ameren Corporation: owner FCF has been negative every year since FY2017 (FY2025: -$803m) because capex (the 5-year plan: $30.5-33.1B as of FY2025, up from $21-22.8B in FY2023) runs well ahead of operating cash flow. This is the capex-supercycle signature of a regulated utility funding rate-base growth, not distress -- OCF itself grew from $2,170m (FY2019) to $3,353m (FY2025), a 7.5% CAGR, and the gap is funded with debt and equity issuance rather than deteriorating operations.

What to watch:

  • OCF growth relative to the capex plan -- OCF funding a shrinking share of capex signals rising external funding need
  • Equity issuance (management guides to ~$5.0bn 2027-31) diluting EPS growth versus rate-base growth

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Ameren Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Ameren Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Ameren Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line across Ameren's four regulated segments (Ameren Missouri electric & gas, Ameren Illinois electric & gas distribution, Ameren Transmission/ATXI).

For Ameren Corporation: revenue includes a pass-through fuel/purchased-power component that earns no return, so it grows more slowly than rate base and earnings (3-yr revenue CAGR 3.4% vs. 8.3% equity CAGR) -- fuel deflation in 2023-24 depressed this line without hurting earnings. Watch allowed ROE and rate-base growth, not revenue growth, as the thesis signal.

What to watch:

  • Rate-case outcomes (Missouri electric case asking $343m, decision expected mid-2027; Illinois MYRP) moving the allowed revenue requirement
  • Large-load/data-center energization lifting volume-driven revenue from 2027
  • Interim rows show seasonality (summer cooling, winter heating)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Ameren Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
